- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially >0.36) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is mildly negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.18) — model ignores downside risk.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to true price drops by 1–2 days, especially after sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to historical mean when sentiment is weak.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in the first 5–7 days after a sentiment spike, then converge — adjust early forecast peaks downward.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is rising (e.g., >0.36), model overreacts; when sentiment is falling (e.g., <0.18), model underreacts — calibrate forecast sensitivity to sentiment magnitude.
